functions.name: _strpbrk
functions.comment:
_strpbrk - Finds first occurrence of any control character in string.

Scans lpszStr for the first character that matches any character in lpszControl.
Uses a 256-bit bitmap for O(1) character set membership testing.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 32-byte (256-bit) bitmap on stack to all zeros via 8 PUSH EAX
2. For each character in lpszControl:
   a. Load character byte value (0-255)
   b. Set corresponding bit using BTS [ESP], EAX instruction
   c. byte_index = char >> 3, bit_position = char & 7
   d. Advance to next character, repeat until null terminator
3. For each character in lpszStr:
   a. Load character byte value
   b. Test corresponding bit using BT [ESP], EAX instruction
   c. If bit is set (CF=1), return pointer to current character
   d. If null terminator reached, return NULL (EAX=0)

Params:
  lpszStr [in] - Pointer to null-terminated string to search
  lpszControl [in] - Pointer to null-terminated character set to match against

Returns:
  char* - Pointer to first matching character in lpszStr
  NULL (0) - If no character from lpszControl found in lpszStr

Special Cases:
  - Empty lpszControl: Returns NULL (no bits set in bitmap)
  - Empty lpszStr: Returns NULL immediately (first char is null terminator)
  - All chars in lpszStr match: Returns pointer to first char

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x20 (32) - Bitmap size in bytes (256 bits covers all byte values)
  >> 3 - Divide by 8 to calculate byte index in bitmap array
  & 7 - Modulo 8 to calculate bit position within byte (0-7)
  BTS - Bit Test and Set: atomically tests and sets bit at computed position
  BT - Bit Test: tests bit at computed position, result in CF flag

Visual Studio C Runtime Library implementation.
Time Complexity: O(m + n) where m = len(lpszControl), n = len(lpszStr)
Space Complexity: O(1) - Fixed 32-byte stack allocation

functions.name: CrtLCMapStringA
functions.signature: int CrtLCMapStringA(LCID dwLocaleId, DWORD dwMapFlags, LPCSTR lpSrcStr, int cchSrc, LPSTR lpDestStr, int cchDest, UINT nCodePage, BOOL fError, int nReserved)
functions.comment:
Maps a character string using locale-specific transformation rules with ANSI/code page conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize SEH frame for exception handling
2. Check g_nLCMapCapability to determine Unicode API availability:
   - 0: Not yet tested - perform capability check using LCMapStringW
   - 1: LCMapStringW is available (Windows NT path)
   - 2: LCMapStringW not available, error 0x78 (Windows 9x path)
3. Calculate actual source string length by scanning for null terminator if cchSrc > 0
4. If Windows NT path (capability = 1):
   a. Get code page from g_pwDefaultCodePage if not specified
   b. Convert ANSI source to wide string via MultiByteToWideChar
   c. Allocate wide buffer on stack or heap based on size
   d. Call LCMapStringW to perform locale mapping on wide string
   e. If LCMAP_SORTKEY flag (0x400) is set, copy result directly
   f. Otherwise convert mapped wide string back to ANSI via WideCharToMultiByte
   g. Free allocated buffers
5. If Windows 9x path (capability = 2 or 0):
   a. Get locale ID from g_nDefaultLocale if not specified
   b. Get code page from g_pwDefaultCodePage if not specified
   c. Call ___ansicp to get ANSI code page for locale
   d. If code pages match, call LCMapStringA directly
   e. Otherwise convert between code pages via ___convertcp
   f. Perform LCMapStringA on converted string
   g. Convert result back to original code page
   h. Free allocated buffers
6. Return character count on success, 0 on failure

Parameters:
  dwLocaleId: LCID locale identifier for mapping (0 = use g_nDefaultLocale)
  dwMapFlags: DWORD mapping flags (LCMAP_LOWERCASE, LCMAP_UPPERCASE, etc.)
              0x400 = LCMAP_SORTKEY (returns sort key bytes)
  lpSrcStr: LPCSTR pointer to source ANSI string to map
  cchSrc: int source string length (-1 for null-terminated)
  lpDestStr: LPSTR pointer to destination buffer (NULL to get required size)
  cchDest: int destination buffer size in characters
  nCodePage: UINT code page for string conversion (0 = use g_pwDefaultCodePage)
  fError: BOOL if TRUE, use MB_ERR_INVALID_CHARS flag for MultiByteToWideChar
  nReserved: int reserved parameter (unused)

Returns:
  int: Number of characters written to lpDestStr on success
       0 on failure (invalid parameters, conversion error, or out of memory)

Special Cases:
  - Capability detection uses LCMapStringW with test string at g_wszCapabilityTest
  - Error 0x78 (ERROR_CALL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED) indicates Windows 9x
  - Stack allocation used for small buffers, heap for larger ones
  - SEH handlers at 0x6fe18106, 0x6fe181d4, 0x6fe18309 for exception cleanup
  - LCMAP_SORTKEY (0x400) bypasses final WideCharToMultiByte conversion

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x100 - LCMAP_LOWERCASE flag for capability test
  0x400 - LCMAP_SORTKEY flag check
  0x78 - ERROR_CALL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED (Windows 9x detection)
  0xffffffff - -1 sentinel for null-terminated string length

functions.name: __fclose_lk
functions.comment:
Standard C Runtime library function - closes a file stream with thread-safe locking.
Library Function: Visual Studio 2003 Release (__fclose_lk maintains standard naming)

Algorithm:
1. Initialize return value to -1 (error state)
2. Check if file stream is valid by testing flags (0x83 = readable|writable|opened)
3. If valid stream:
   a. Flush any pending output data to underlying file
   b. Free internal stream buffers using __freebuf
   c. Close underlying file descriptor via FUN_6ff31a7d
   d. If close fails, set return value to -1
   e. If temporary filename exists, deallocate it and clear pointer
4. Clear all file stream flags to mark as closed
5. Return result code (0 = success, -1 = error)

Parameters:
pFile - Pointer to FILE structure representing the stream to close

Returns:
0 on successful closure of all resources
-1 if any cleanup operation fails (flush, buffer free, or file descriptor close)

Special Cases:
If FILE._flag & 0x83 == 0, stream is already closed - skip cleanup, only clear flags
If FILE._tmpfname is NULL, no temporary file to deallocate
Function always clears _flag to 0 regardless of cleanup success/failure

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x83 (131) - FILE flag mask for stream validity (readable|writable|opened bits)
0x0C (12)  - Offset to FILE._flag field in FILE structure  
0x10 (16)  - Offset to FILE._file field (underlying file descriptor)
0x1C (28)  - Offset to FILE._tmpfname field (temporary filename pointer)

Error Handling:
FlushOutputBuffer failure: Continues with cleanup, final result depends on file close
FUN_6ff31a7d (file close) failure: Sets nResult to -1, continues with temp file cleanup
DeallocateMemory failure: Not checked, assumes successful deallocation

functions.name: _fclose
functions.comment:
Closes an open file stream and releases associated resources.

Algorithm:
  1. Initialize return value nResult to -1 (error)
  2. Check if file has the 0x40 flag set (indicates string stream or special mode)
  3. If flag NOT set (normal file):
     a. Lock the file stream for thread safety
     b. Call __fclose_lk to perform the actual close operation
     c. Unlock the file stream
  4. If flag IS set (special stream):
     a. Clear the file flag to 0 (mark as closed without full cleanup)
  5. Return nResult (0 on success, -1 on failure)

Parameters:
  pFile [FILE *] - Pointer to FILE structure representing the stream to close.
                   Must be a valid open file pointer from fopen/freopen.

Returns:
  int - 0 on successful close, -1 (EOF) on error or if stream was not valid.

Notes:
  - Thread-safe: Uses file locking for multi-threaded access
  - The 0x40 flag typically indicates a string stream (_IOSTRG) which has special handling
  - After fclose, the FILE pointer is invalid and must not be used
  - Library function from Visual Studio 2003 Release

functions.name: UnlockFileFromEsi
functions.comment: Unlocks a FILE stream using the ESI register as an implicit parameter. This is an epilog thunk called after _fclose_lk completes. The FILE pointer is preserved in the ESI register by the calling function (_fclose) during the __lock_file call, allowing this function to unlock without explicit parameter passing. Algorithm: 1. Retrieve FILE pointer from ESI register (set by caller) 2. Call __unlock_file to release the stream lock 3. Return to caller. Parameters: IMPLICIT in_ESI (FILE*) - Pointer to FILE stream to unlock. Returns: void. Callers: _fclose - Called after __fclose_lk to release the lock acquired by __lock_file. Notes: This is a common CRT pattern where the epilog unlock is separated from the main close logic to allow proper exception handling and stack unwinding.

functions.name: FlushFileDescriptor
functions.comment:
Flushes OS file buffers for a file descriptor and handles error reporting through thread-local errno.

Algorithm:
1. Validate file descriptor against g_dwMaxFileDescriptor limit
2. If invalid, set errno to EBADF (0x9) and return -1
3. Calculate stride offset: (fdFile & 0x1f) * 0x24 for validation array access
4. Load validation bitmap from g_FileDescriptorTable[fdFile >> 5]
5. Test bit 0 of validation byte at [bitmap + 4 + stride] to check if descriptor active
6. If not active, jump to error handler
7. Lock file descriptor using __lock_fhandle(fdFile) to prevent concurrent access
8. Re-verify file descriptor validity after lock acquired (race condition check)
9. If still valid, obtain OS file handle via __get_osfhandle(fdFile)
10. Call Windows FlushFileBuffers API to flush file buffers to disk
11. Check flush result: 0=failure (GetLastError), non-zero=success
12. If error occurred, retrieve Windows error code and store in thread-local errno
13. If no error, errorCode remains 0
14. Unlock file descriptor via __unlock_fhandle(fdFile)
15. Return errorCode: 0 on success, system error code on Windows API failure, -1 (0xffffffff) on validation/locking failure

Parameters:
fdFile (uint) - File descriptor to flush, typically obtained from FILE structure _file member (0-based index into descriptor table)

Returns:
int - 0 on successful flush, system error code (non-zero DWORD) if Windows API failed, -1 (0xffffffff) if descriptor invalid or locking failed

Special Cases:
- File descriptors are validated through a bitmap array where bit 0 indicates active status
- Validation is performed twice: before and after acquiring lock to detect descriptor closure during lock wait
- Stride calculation (fd & 0x1f) * 0x24 suggests up to 32 descriptors per table entry, each with 0x24 bytes storage
- EBADF (0x9) is standard POSIX error for bad file descriptor
- Thread-local errno access via GetThreadErrorNumberPointer() supports multi-threaded error handling
- Lock/unlock pair ensures atomic flush operation without descriptor state corruption

functions.name: UnlockFileHandleThunk
functions.comment:
C runtime file handle unlock thunk wrapper

Algorithm:

functions.name: __resetstkoflw
functions.comment:
Reset Stack Overflow Protection

Recovers from a stack overflow exception by resetting the guard page at the bottom
of the stack. This function is part of the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime library
and is called after catching a EXCEPTION_STACK_OVERFLOW structured exception.

Algorithm:
1. Query memory info for current stack pointer using VirtualQuery on stack frame
2. Get system page size via GetSystemInfo
3. Calculate stack page boundary by aligning stack pointer to page and subtracting one page
4. Compute guard page location based on OS version:
   - Windows NT/2000: 17 pages from allocation base
   - Windows 9x: 2 pages from allocation base (0x11 vs 0x2)
5. Verify stack page is above guard page boundary (stack grows down)
6. For Windows NT/2000:
   a. Walk committed memory regions from allocation base via VirtualQuery loop
   b. Find first committed region (MEM_COMMIT = 0x1000)
   c. Check if PAGE_GUARD (0x100) is already set - if so, return success
   d. Verify target page is reachable from current stack position
   e. Commit memory at guard page location via VirtualAlloc with PAGE_READWRITE
7. Set new page protection via VirtualProtect:
   - Windows NT/2000: PAGE_READWRITE | PAGE_GUARD (0x104)
   - Windows 9x: PAGE_READWRITE (0x04)

Parameters:
   (none) - Uses current stack frame to determine recovery location

Returns:
   int - Non-zero (TRUE) on success, 0 (FALSE) on failure
   Success indicates guard page was successfully restored
   Failure cases:
   - VirtualQuery fails on stack pointer
   - Stack is above minimum protected region
   - Cannot find committed memory region (NT only)
   - Stack already below committed region
   - VirtualProtect fails to set guard page

Special Cases:
- Windows 9x (g_dwOsVersionType == 1): Simpler path without memory region walking
- Windows NT/2000: Full memory region analysis before restoring guard
- Already protected: Returns 1 if PAGE_GUARD already set on committed region

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1c = sizeof(MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION) on 32-bit
0x1000 = MEM_COMMIT (memory state for committed pages)
0x100 = PAGE_GUARD protection flag
0x104 = PAGE_READWRITE | PAGE_GUARD (NT protection)
0x11 = 17 pages offset for NT guard region
0xfffffff1 = Mask to compute guard offset based on OS type

Error Handling:
All API failures return 0. No exceptions are raised.

functions.name: CloseFileDescriptorLocked
functions.comment:
Closes a file descriptor and releases associated OS handle resources.

This is a low-level CRT function that performs file descriptor cleanup
while holding a lock (hence the _lk suffix). It handles the special case
of stdout/stderr sharing the same OS handle.

Algorithm:
1. Get the OS handle for the file descriptor via __get_osfhandle
2. If handle is invalid (-1), skip to cleanup
3. For stdout (fd=1) or stderr (fd=2), check if they share the same OS handle
4. If stdout and stderr share handles, skip CloseHandle to avoid double-close
5. Call CloseHandle on the OS handle
6. If CloseHandle fails, capture error via GetLastError
7. Free the OS handle slot via __free_osfhnd
8. Clear the file descriptor flags in the I/O info table
9. If an error occurred, map it to errno via __dosmaperr and return -1
10. Return 0 on success

Params:
  nFileDescriptor (uint): C runtime file descriptor index (0-2047)

Returns:
  0: Success - file descriptor closed and resources freed
  -1: Failure - errno set via __dosmaperr, GetLastError preserved

Special Cases:
  - Invalid handle (INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE): Silently succeeds without CloseHandle
  - stdout/stderr sharing: Skips CloseHandle to prevent double-close bugs

Magic Numbers:
  0x24 (36): Size of ioinfo structure in the I/O table
  0x1f (31): Mask for extracting slot index within table segment (5-bit)
  >> 5: Division by 32 to get table segment index
  +4: Offset to flags byte within ioinfo structure

Structure Layout (g_ppIoInfo):
  Offset  Size  Field       Type        Description
  0x00    4     osHandle    HANDLE      Windows OS file handle
  0x04    1     osFlags     byte        File descriptor state flags
  ...     ...   ...         ...         (other ioinfo fields)
  (Total size: 0x24 bytes per entry)

Error Handling:
  CloseHandle failure -> GetLastError -> __dosmaperr -> errno set -> return -1

functions.name: CloseFileDescriptor
functions.comment:
Closes a file descriptor and releases associated OS handle resources.

This is the main entry point for the CRT _close() function. It validates
the file handle, acquires locks for thread safety, and delegates to
CloseFileDescriptorLocked for the actual close operation.

Algorithm:
1. Validate file handle is within valid range (< g_dwMaxFileHandles)
2. Calculate ioinfo table slot: segment = fd >> 5, offset = (fd & 0x1f) * 0x24
3. Check if file descriptor has FOPEN flag (bit 0) set
4. Acquire lock via LockFileHandle for thread-safe access
5. Re-check FOPEN flag after acquiring lock (race condition check)
6. If flag cleared during lock acquisition, set errno=EBADF(9), return -1
7. Otherwise call CloseFileDescriptorLocked to perform actual close
8. Release lock via UnlockFileHandleThunk and return result

Parameters:
  nFileHandle (int): C runtime file descriptor index (0-2047)
    Must be < g_dwMaxFileHandles and have FOPEN flag set

Returns:
  0: Success - file descriptor closed and resources freed
  -1: Failure with errno set:
    - EBADF (9): Invalid file handle or not open

Special Cases:
  - Invalid handle (>= g_dwMaxFileHandles): Returns -1, errno=EBADF, doserrno=0
  - Not open (FOPEN bit clear): Returns -1, errno=EBADF, doserrno=0
  - Race condition (closed by another thread): Returns -1, errno=EBADF

Magic Numbers:
  0x24 (36): Size of ioinfo structure in I/O table
  0x1f (31): Mask for slot index within 32-entry segment
  >> 5: Division by 32 to get segment index
  +4: Offset to osFlags byte within ioinfo structure
  & 1: FOPEN flag - indicates file descriptor is open
  9: EBADF - Bad file descriptor errno value

Structure Layout (g_ppIoInfo segments):
  Offset  Size  Field       Type    Description
  0x00    4     osHandle    HANDLE  Windows OS file handle
  0x04    1     osFlags     byte    File descriptor state flags
  (Total size: 0x24 bytes per entry, 32 entries per segment)

Decompiler Temporaries:
  nSlotOffset: Byte offset into ioinfo array = (fd & 0x1f) * 0x24
  pErrno: Pointer to errno thread-local storage

functions.name: ConvertToLowerMt
functions.comment:
Converts a character to lowercase using locale-aware mapping.

This is a multithreaded-safe version of the tolower function from the Visual Studio 2003 CRT.
It handles both ASCII and multibyte characters using the locale-specific mapping tables.

Algorithm:
1. Check if locale handle is null or character is ASCII (< 0x80) with SBCS optimization
2. For simple ASCII uppercase A-Z (0x41-0x5A), return character + 0x20
3. For extended characters (>= 0x100), check if character is uppercase via ctype table
4. If character byte count > 1, use ___isctype_mt to check character type
5. Build multibyte character buffer based on lead byte flag (0x80 in ctype table)
6. Call CrtLCMapStringA with LCMAP_LOWERCASE (0x100) to perform conversion
7. Return mapped character, handling both single and double byte results

Parameters:
  pLocaleInfo - Pointer to threadlocaleinfostruct containing locale data
              - Offset 0x14: LCID locale identifier (0 = C locale)
              - Offset 0x24: wlocale pointer (non-null = SBCS optimization available)
              - Offset 0x28: lc_category[1].refcount (byte count indicator)
              - Offset 0x48: lc_category[3].refcount (character type table pointer)
              - Offset 0x04: Code page (passed to CrtLCMapStringA)
  dwCharacter - Character to convert (can be single byte or lead/trail byte pair)

Returns:
  uint - Lowercase equivalent of input character
       - Returns input unchanged if not uppercase or conversion fails
       - For ASCII A-Z: returns character + 0x20 (a-z)
       - For single-byte result: lower 8 bits of output buffer
       - For double-byte result: combined high/low bytes from output buffer

Magic Numbers:
  0x80 - ASCII range limit for SBCS optimization
  0x100 - LCMAP_LOWERCASE flag for LCMapStringA
  0x41 - ASCII 'A'
  0x5A - ASCII 'Z'
  0x20 - Offset to convert uppercase to lowercase

Moves structure field data from source to destination with field remapping.

Copies specific fields from a source structure (pwSrc in EAX) to destination
(pDest in ECX) with different offset mappings, then clears the source pointer
field to indicate ownership transfer. This is a move operation, not a copy.

Algorithm:
1. Copy word from source offset 0x0 to destination offset 0x0
2. Copy word from source offset 0x2 to destination offset 0x2
3. Copy byte from source offset 0x4 to destination offset 0x6
4. Copy byte from source offset 0x5 to destination offset 0x7
5. Copy word from source offset 0x6 to destination offset 0x8
6. Copy word from source offset 0x8 to destination offset 0xA
7. Copy dword from source offset 0xC to destination offset 0x10
8. Clear source dword at offset 0xC to zero (ownership transfer)

Parameters:
  pDest (ECX, byte*): Pointer to destination structure buffer, minimum 20 bytes
  IMPLICIT pwSrc (EAX, ushort*): Pointer to source structure, 16 bytes used

Returns:
  void - No return value

Field Mapping Table:
  Source    Size    Destination
  0x00      2       0x00
  0x02      2       0x02
  0x04      1       0x06
  0x05      1       0x07
  0x06      2       0x08
  0x08      2       0x0A
  0x0C      4       0x10

Note: The source field at offset 0x0C is cleared to zero after copying,
indicating this is a move operation that transfers ownership of a pointer
or reference count from source to destination structure.

functions.name: IsColorArrayVaried
functions.comment:
Checks if a color array contains any entry different from a reference RGB color.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize loop counter to 0
2. Compare each 3-byte RGB entry against the reference color:
   - Byte 0: Low byte of dwRgbColor (Red)
   - Byte 1: Second byte of dwRgbColor (Green)
   - Byte 2: Third byte of dwRgbColor (Blue)
3. If any byte mismatches, return true (array has varied colors)
4. Advance pointer by 3 bytes and increment counter
5. If all 512 entries match, return false (array is uniform)

Parameters:
  pColorArray (IMPLICIT via EAX): Pointer to array of 3-byte RGB color entries
  dwRgbColor: Reference RGB color packed as uint (R=bits 0-7, G=bits 8-15, B=bits 16-23)

Returns:
  true (1): Found at least one different color in the array
  false (0): All 512 entries match the reference color

Magic Numbers:
  0x200 (512): Maximum entries to check (512 * 3 = 1536 bytes)
  3: Bytes per RGB color entry

Notes:
  Uses custom calling convention with EAX as implicit input parameter.
  Commonly used to detect if a color palette has variation.

functions.name: ValidateEmptyAutomapCell
functions.signature: bool ValidateEmptyAutomapCell(void * this, byte * pbCellData, int nStride)
functions.comment:
ValidateEmptyAutomapCell - Checks if automap cell contains only transparent/empty pixels

Algorithm:
1. If transparency flag (bit 1) set in config flags at [EAX+0x51]:
   - Iterate 32x32 pixels, reading 3-byte RGB values
   - Compare each pixel (masked 0xFFFFFF) against transparency color at [EAX+0x34]
   - Return false if any pixel differs from transparency color
2. If alpha flag (bit 0) set in config flags at [EAX+0x51]:
   - Iterate 32x32 pixels, reading 1-byte alpha values
   - Return false if any alpha byte is non-zero
3. Return true if all checks pass (cell is empty/transparent)

Parameters:
  this (ECX)     - byte* - Pointer to pixel data buffer (32x32 cell)
  pbCellData     - byte* - Unused (stride passed through param_1 in caller)
  nStride        - int   - Row stride in bytes (distance between rows)
  IMPLICIT EAX   - AutomapConfig* - Configuration structure with transparency settings

Returns:
  bool - true if cell is empty/transparent and should be skipped
         false if cell contains visible content to be added

Structure Layout (AutomapConfig at EAX):
  Offset  Size  Field              Description
  0x34    3     dwTransparencyRGB  Transparency color (RGB, 24-bit)
  0x51    1     bValidationFlags   Validation mode flags
                                   Bit 0: Check alpha (pixels must be 0)
                                   Bit 1: Check RGB transparency match

Magic Numbers:
  0x20 (32)     - Tile dimension (32x32 pixels)
  0x60 (96)     - RGB row size (32 pixels * 3 bytes)
  0xFFFFFF      - 24-bit RGB mask

Caller Context:
  Called from AddAutomapCell at 6fe1a20e to skip empty cells

functions.name: CreateTileCmpContext
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a TileCmp context structure (109 bytes).

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x6D (109) bytes via Fog_MemAlloc
2. If allocation fails, call CleanupAndAbort with error context
3. Zero-initialize the first 16 bytes of the structure (4 DWORDs)
4. Store dwTileParam1 at offset 0x00
5. Store dwTileParam2 at offset 0x04
6. Return pointer to allocated context

Parameters:
  dwTileParam1 [Stack+0x04] - First tile parameter (stored at context offset 0x00)
  dwTileParam2 [Stack+0x08] - Second tile parameter (stored at context offset 0x04)

Returns:
  Success: Pointer to initialized TileCmpContext structure (109 bytes)
  Failure: Does not return (calls CleanupAndAbort)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x6D (109) - Size of TileCmpContext structure in bytes
  0x6E (110) - Source line number for error reporting
  0x6fe2ec35 - Error code/string pointer for CleanupAndAbort
  0x6fe2f04c - Source file: ..\Source\D2CMP\SRC\Tilecmp.cpp

Structure Layout (TileCmpContext):
  Offset  Size  Field         Type    Description
  0x00    4     dwParam1      uint    First tile parameter
  0x04    4     dwParam2      uint    Second tile parameter
  0x08    4     dwField3      uint    Reserved (initialized to 0)
  0x0C    4     dwField4      uint    Reserved (initialized to 0)
  0x10    93    abData        byte[]  Additional context data

Error Handling:
  On allocation failure, CleanupAndAbort is called with:
  - Error code: 0x6fe2ec35 (FastCmp related error path)
  - Return address context
  - Line number: 0x6E (110)
  ReportError(-1) is also called but never reached

functions.name: AllocateAndInitializeSkillData
functions.comment:
Allocates and zero-initializes a 96-byte skill data structure.

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10042 to allocate 0x60 (96) bytes with type ID 0x45
2. If allocation fails (returns NULL):
   a. Get current return address for error context
   b. Call CleanupAndAbort with error code 0x6fe2ec35
   c. Call ReportError with -1 (does not return)
3. Zero-initialize all 24 dwords (0x18 * 4 = 96 bytes) using REP STOSD
4. Return pointer to allocated and initialized structure

Parameters: None

Returns:
  - void*: Pointer to allocated and zeroed 96-byte structure on success
  - Does not return on allocation failure (calls error handlers)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x45     - Memory allocation type ID (skill data)
  0x60     - Allocation size (96 bytes)
  0x18     - DWORD count for zeroing (24 dwords = 96 bytes)
  0x46     - Source line number for error reporting
  0x6fe2ec35 - Error code passed to CleanupAndAbort

Error Handling:
  Allocation failure triggers cleanup sequence and program abort

functions.name: FreeTileComponentNode
functions.comment:
FreeTileComponentNode - Frees a tile component node and its optional callback data.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pTileNode (IMPLICIT in ESI) is non-null
   - If null, abort via CleanupAndAbort with source line 0x31
2. Check if node has callback data at [pTileNode 0xc]
   - If callback exists, call InitializeModule with opcode 0x35 to free it
3. Call InitializeModule with opcode 0x38 to free the node itself
4. Return

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT ESI pTileNode - Pointer to tile component node to free

Returns:
  void - No return value (aborts on null input)

Special Cases:
  NULL pTileNode triggers abort via CleanupAndAbort (line 0x31)

Structure Layout (TileComponentNode):
  Offset  Size  Field       Type    Description
  0x0c    4     pCallback   void*   Optional callback/sub-data pointer

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x31 - Source line number for null check abort
  0x35 - InitializeModule opcode (free callback data)
  0x38 - InitializeModule opcode (free node)
  0x6fe2f04c - szFile: ..\Source\D2CMP\SRC\Tilecmp.cpp
  0x6fe2ec35 - Error code for CleanupAndAbort

Related Functions:
  ProcessTileComponentNodes (6fe1a3f0) - Processes list of tile nodes using same opcodes

functions.name: AllocAutomapCellEntry
functions.comment:
AllocAutomapCellEntry - Allocates and initializes an automap cell entry structure

Algorithm:
1. Call Fog_MemAlloc with allocation ID 0x23 to allocate 0x14 (20) bytes for cell entry
2. If allocation fails, abort with error code 0x24
3. Zero-initialize all 5 dwords of the structure
4. Return pointer to the allocated and initialized cell entry

Parameters:
  (none)

Returns:
  AuCelList* - Pointer to newly allocated and zero-initialized cell entry

Magic Numbers:
  0x23 - Allocation ID for Fog_MemAlloc
  0x14 - Size in bytes (20 = 5 dwords)
  0x24 - Error code for allocation failure

Structure Layout (AuCelList, 0x14 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field         Type    Description
  0x00    4     dwBase        uint    Base value (initialized to 0)
  0x04    4     pNext         void*   Next cell in list
  0x08    4     pPrev         void*   Previous cell in list
  0x0C    4     dwReserved1   uint    Reserved field 1
  0x10    4     dwReserved2   uint    Reserved field 2

functions.name: IterateTileCellData
functions.comment:
Iterates through tile cell data and invokes a callback for each packed RGB value.

This function processes a hierarchical tile context structure containing groups of cell data. For each cell element, it extracts packed 3-byte RGB values and calls the provided callback function with each unpacked 24-bit color value.

Algorithm:
  1. Validate pTileContext is non-NULL (error 0x3EA if NULL)
  2. Check initialization flag at offset +0x4 (bit 0 must be set, error 0x3EB otherwise)
  3. Iterate through nGroupCount groups (offset +0x10C), each 0x60 bytes apart
  4. For each group, iterate through nSubElementCount elements (offset +0x50), each 0x14 bytes
  5. For each element, read byte count (offset +0xA) and RGB data pointer (offset +0x10)
  6. Unpack 3-byte RGB triplets and invoke callback with 24-bit color value
  7. The division by 3 calculates iteration count from byte count

Parameters:
  pTileContext (TileCellContext*) - Pointer to tile context structure with groups array
  pfnCallback (CellDataCallback*) - Callback function invoked as: pfnCallback(uint dwPackedRgb)

Returns:
  void - Returns normally on success, aborts on validation failure

Error Handling:
  0x3EA - NULL context pointer
  0x3EB - Context not properly initialized (flag bit 0 not set)

Structure Layout (TileCellContext):
  +0x004  byte    fFlags              Initialization flags (bit 0 = initialized)
  +0x10C  int     nGroupCount         Number of cell groups
  +0x110  void*   pGroupArray         Pointer to array of 0x60-byte group structures

Group Structure (0x60 bytes each):
  +0x050  int     nSubElementCount    Number of sub-elements in group
  +0x054  void*   pSubElementData     Pointer to sub-element array

Sub-Element Structure (0x14 bytes each):
  +0x00A  ushort  wDataByteCount      Byte count of RGB data (multiple of 3)
  +0x010  byte*   pbRgbData           Pointer to packed 3-byte RGB values

Magic Numbers:
  0x3EA (1002) - Error code for NULL context
  0x3EB (1003) - Error code for uninitialized context
  0x60 (96) - Group structure stride
  0x14 (20) - Sub-element structure stride
  0xAAAAAAAB - Magic constant for division by 3 optimization

functions.name: RebaseStructurePointers
functions.comment:
Rebases relative offset pointers to absolute addresses in a resource entry array.

Called after loading resource data where internal pointers are stored as relative
offsets. Iterates through each 0x14-byte entry and converts the offset at  0x10
to an absolute pointer by adding the base address.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pResourceContext is not NULL (abort with error 0x3C9 if NULL)
2. Get base pointer from pResourceContext 0x54
3. Get entry count from pResourceContext 0x50
4. For each entry (0x14 bytes each):
   a. Read relative offset at entry 0x10
   b. Add base pointer to convert to absolute address
   c. Store absolute pointer back at entry 0x10

Parameters:
  pResourceContext (ECX) - Pointer to resource context structure
     0x50: Entry count (int)
     0x54: Pointer to base of entry array / base address for rebasing

Returns: void

Error Handling:
  If pResourceContext is NULL, calls CleanupAndAbort with error code 0x3C9

Structure Layout (Entry at pResourceContext 0x54):
  Offset  Size  Type   Description
  0x00    0x10  -      Unknown fields
  0x10    0x04  int*   Relative offset converted to absolute pointer
  0x14    -     -      Next entry

Magic Numbers:
  0x3C9 (969) - Error code for NULL resource context
  0x14  (20)  - Size of each entry in array
  0x50  (80)  - Offset to entry count in context
  0x54  (84)  - Offset to entry array pointer in context

functions.name: Ordinal_10083
functions.signature: undefined Ordinal_10083(int * param_1, undefined4 * param_2, char * param_3)

functions.name: SerializeSpriteDataToBuffer
functions.signature: void SerializeSpriteDataToBuffer(void * this, void * pSpriteData, void * * ppDestBuffer, uint * pnBufferSize)
functions.comment:
Serializes a sprite data structure into a contiguous buffer for storage or transmission.

This function creates a deep copy of a sprite structure (SpriteData) into a newly allocated
buffer, converting all internal pointers to relative offsets. The output buffer is self-contained
and suitable for file storage or network transfer.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters (null checks with error codes 0x2D9-0x2DB)
2. Verify source has frames (offset +0x10C \!= 0, error 0x2DC if zero)
3. Calculate total buffer size via CalculateSpriteBufferSize
4. Allocate buffer via Ordinal_10042 (allocation with line 0x2E3)
5. Zero-initialize the allocated buffer
6. Copy base header (0x45 dwords = 0x114 bytes)
7. Copy frame entry array (nFrameCount * 0x60 bytes each)
8. Update frame data offset to relative position (offset +0x110)
9. For each frame: copy frame data via CopySpriteFrameEntries
10. Update source flags (|= 2) and dest flags (|= 6)

Parameters:
  this (ECX) - Sprite system context (unused, passed to size calculator)
  pSpriteData - Pointer to source SpriteData structure:
    +0x004: dwFlags - Status flags (bit 1 set on serialization)
    +0x10C: nFrameCount - Number of frames in sprite
    +0x110: pFrameData - Pointer to frame entry array
  ppDestBuffer - Output: receives pointer to allocated serialized buffer
  pnBufferSize - Output: receives total size of serialized buffer

Returns:
  void - Errors trigger CleanupAndAbort with ReportError(-1)

Error Codes (line numbers):
  0x2D9 (729) - pSpriteData is NULL
  0x2DA (730) - ppDestBuffer is NULL
  0x2DB (731) - pnBufferSize is NULL
  0x2DC (732) - Source has no frames (nFrameCount == 0)
  0x2E0 (736) - Size calculation returned 0
  0x2E4 (740) - Memory allocation failed

Structure Layout (SpriteData):
  Offset | Size | Field        | Type    | Description
  0x000  | 0x04 | dwReserved   | uint    | Reserved/unknown
  0x004  | 0x04 | dwFlags      | uint    | Status flags (bit 1 = serialized)
  0x008  | 0x104| abHeader     | byte[]  | Header data (0x41 dwords)
  0x10C  | 0x04 | nFrameCount  | int     | Number of frame entries
  0x110  | 0x04 | pFrameData   | void*   | Pointer to frame entry array

Structure Layout (Serialized Buffer):
  Offset | Size      | Field         | Description
  0x000  | 0x114     | Header        | Copy of source header (0x45 dwords)
  0x114  | N*0x60    | FrameEntries  | Array of frame entries
  0x114+N*0x60 | var | FrameData     | Concatenated frame pixel data

Flag Bits:
  Bit 1 (0x02) - Set on source after serialization
  Bit 1 (0x02) - Set on dest buffer
  Bit 2 (0x04) - Set on dest buffer (serialized format indicator)

functions.name: CopyDirectionData
functions.comment:
Copies animation direction data from a source direction structure to a destination buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Copy base offset field from pSrcDir+0x10 to pDstDir+0x00
2. Copy two 16-bit fields (flags) from pSrcDir+0x14,0x16 to pDstDir+0x04,0x06
3. Calculate width (pSrcDir[2]-pSrcDir[0]) and height (pSrcDir[3]-pSrcDir[1]) deltas
4. Copy 5 dword fields from pSrcDir+0x24..0x34 to pDstDir+0x14..0x24
5. Copy 25 bytes from pSrcDir+0x38 to pDstDir+0x28 (animation data)
6. Copy layer count from pSrcDir+0x54 to pDstDir+0x50
7. Allocate contiguous array for layers (count * 0x14 bytes)
8. Traverse linked list at pSrcDir+0x58 copying each 0x14-byte layer entry
9. Validate layer count matches expected, abort on mismatch

Parameters:
  pDstDir (Stack[0x4]) - Pointer to destination direction buffer (0x60 bytes)
  IMPLICIT pSrcDir (EAX) - Pointer to source direction structure

Returns:
  void (aborts on allocation failure or layer count mismatch)

Error Handling:
  0x201 - Memory allocation request code
  0x202 - Layer array allocation failed
  0x213 - Layer count mismatch after copy
  Calls CleanupAndAbort with file marker 0x6fe2ec35

Source Direction Structure Layout (via EAX):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x00    4     nMinX           Bounding box minimum X
  0x04    4     nMinY           Bounding box minimum Y  
  0x08    4     nMaxX           Bounding box maximum X
  0x0C    4     nMaxY           Bounding box maximum Y
  0x10    4     dwBaseOffset    Base frame offset
  0x14    2     wFlags1         Direction flags 1
  0x16    2     wFlags2         Direction flags 2
  0x24-34 20    dwFields[5]     Animation parameters
  0x38    25    abData          Animation byte data
  0x54    4     nLayerCount     Number of layers
  0x58    4     pLayerList      Linked list head of layer entries

Destination Direction Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x00    4     dwBaseOffset    Copied from src+0x10
  0x04    2     wFlags1         Copied from src+0x14
  0x06    2     wFlags2         Copied from src+0x16
  0x08    4     nHeight         src[3] - src[1]
  0x0C    4     nWidth          src[2] - src[0]
  0x14-24 20    dwFields[5]     Copied from src+0x24
  0x28    25    abData          Copied from src+0x38
  0x50    4     nLayerCount     Layer count
  0x54    4     pLayers         Allocated layer array

Layer Entry Structure (0x14 bytes each):
  Offset  Size  Field
  0x00    2     word field 1
  0x02    2     word field 2
  0x06    1     byte field
  0x07    1     byte field
  0x08    2     word field 3
  0x0A    2     word field 4
  0x10    4     dword field (cleared in source after copy)

functions.name: ExtractPaletteLayerGrid
functions.signature: void ExtractPaletteLayerGrid(ColorPalette * pLayerResult, byte * pSourcePalette, uint dwBackgroundColor, uint nSourceIndex)
functions.comment:
Extracts a diamond-shaped region from a palette source and stores it in a layer buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x154 (340) bytes buffer via Ordinal_10042 (memory allocation)
2. If allocation fails, call CleanupAndAbort with line 0x155 and ReportError(-1)
3. Zero-initialize the buffer (0x180 dwords = 1536 bytes = 0x600 bytes)
4. Fill all 0x200 (512) entries with 3-byte background color from dwBackgroundColor
5. Calculate source offset: pSourcePalette + (in_EAX * 0xA0 + nSourceIndex) * 3
6. Copy palette data in a diamond pattern over 15 rows:
   - Rows 0-6: Column offset starts at 0x2A, decreases by 6 per row; copy size 0xC to 0x54 bytes
   - Rows 7-14: Column offset increases by 6 per row; copy size 0x54 to 0xC bytes
   - Source row stride: 0x1E0 (480 bytes); Dest row stride: 0x60 (96 bytes)
7. Validate all 512 entries still contain background color
8. If validation passes (all background): call InitializeModule and return
9. If mismatch found: set flags 0x2001 at result+6, store buffer at result+0xC, set size 0x600 at result+8

Parameters:
  pLayerResult: ColorPalette* - Output structure to receive layer data and status flags
  pSourcePalette: byte* - Source palette data buffer (contains full palette image)
  dwBackgroundColor: uint - 3-byte RGB color value to use as background fill
  nSourceIndex: uint - Column offset index into source palette data
  IMPLICIT in_EAX: int - Layer/row index multiplier for source offset calculation

Returns:
  void - Result stored in pLayerResult structure
  - If all entries match background: function returns after cleanup (empty layer)
  - If non-background entries found: pLayerResult receives buffer pointer and flags

Special Cases:
  - Memory allocation failure triggers fatal error via CleanupAndAbort
  - Diamond pattern copies variable-width strips centered on each row
  - Pattern is symmetric around row 7 (widest point)
  - Validation scan checks all 512 3-byte entries against original background

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x154 (340): Allocation size for buffer structure header
  0x600 (1536): Total palette entry data size (512 entries x 3 bytes)
  0x200 (512): Number of palette entries
  0x2A (42): Initial column offset in bytes
  0x1E0 (480): Source palette row stride
  0x60 (96): Destination buffer row stride
  0x2001: Flags indicating layer contains valid data

ColorPalette Structure Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field      | Type   | Description
  -------|------|------------|--------|----------------------------------
  +0x00  | 4    | dwField0   | dword  | Reserved/padding
  +0x04  | 4    | dwField1   | dword  | Contains flags at high word
  +0x06  | 2    | wFlags     | ushort | Layer status flags (0x2001 = has data)
  +0x08  | 2    | wSize      | ushort | Layer data size (0x600)
  +0x0A  | 2    | reserved   | ushort | Padding
  +0x0C  | 4    | dwField3   | dword  | Pointer to palette buffer data
  Total Size: 0x14 (20 bytes)

functions.name: AddAutomapCell
functions.signature: void AddAutomapCell(AURGNBaseObject * pAutomap, byte * pbCellData, int nStride, int nCellX, int nCellY)
functions.comment:
AddAutomapCell - Adds a new cell to the automap display region

Algorithm:
1. Validate pAutomap pointer (error 0x100 if NULL)
2. Validate pbCellData pointer (error 0x101 if NULL)
3. Call FUN_6fe19940 to validate cell data against transparency/visibility flags
4. Allocate new cell entry (0x14 bytes) via FUN_6fe19ad0
5. Link cell entry to automap linked list (pAutomap[2].pHeadPtr)
6. Increment cell count (pAutomap[2].nNodeCount)
7. Validate coordinates are within 16-bit range (error 0x112 if >= 0x10000)
8. Store cell coordinates (X at offset 0, Y at offset 2)
9. Allocate pixel buffer (0xC00 bytes = 96x32 pixels)
10. Zero-initialize pixel buffer (0x300 dwords = 3072 bytes)
11. Configure cell entry: size=0xC00, flags=0x1001
12. Copy 32 rows of 96 bytes (0x60) from source with stride
13. Update automap bounding box (min/max X and Y coordinates)

Parameters:
  pAutomap    - AURGNBaseObject* - Automap region structure containing bounding box and cell list
  pbCellData  - byte*           - Source pixel data for the cell (32x32 with stride)
  nStride     - int             - Row stride of source data (bytes between rows)
  nCellX      - int             - X coordinate of cell in world space
  nCellY      - int             - Y coordinate of cell in world space

Returns:
  void - No return value; aborts on allocation failure

Error Codes (passed to CleanupAndAbort):
  0x100 - NULL pAutomap pointer
  0x101 - NULL pbCellData pointer
  0x109 - Cell entry allocation failed
  0x112 - Coordinate out of range (>= 0x10000)
  0x11a - Pixel buffer allocation failed

Structure Layout (Cell Entry at pCellEntry, 0x14 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field         Description
  0x00    2     nX            Cell X coordinate (world space)
  0x02    2     nY            Cell Y coordinate (world space)
  0x06    2     wFlags        Cell flags (0x1001 = active)
  0x08    2     wBufferSize   Pixel buffer size (0xC00)
  0x0C    4     pbPixels      Pointer to pixel buffer
  0x10    4     pNext         Next cell in linked list

Magic Numbers:
  0x10000  - Maximum coordinate value (65536, 16-bit limit)
  0x119    - Allocation ID for Fog_MemAlloc (pixel buffer)
  0xC00    - Pixel buffer size (3072 bytes = 32x96)
  0x300    - Loop count for zero init (768 dwords = 3072 bytes)
  0x20     - Tile size in pixels (32x32)
  0x60     - Bytes per row copied (96 = 32 pixels * 3 bytes/pixel)

functions.name: AllocateAndLinkListNode
functions.signature: void * AllocateAndLinkListNode(void * pListHead, ushort wNodeType, ushort wFlags, uint dwParam4, uint dwParam5, uint dwParam6, uint dwParam7, uint dwParam8, void * pCopyData)
functions.comment:
Allocates a 0x60-byte node and links it into a doubly-linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pListHead is non-null, abort with error 0xA2 if null
2. Call Ordinal_10042 (Fog.GetItemData) to allocate 0x60-byte node (type 0x45)
3. If allocation fails, abort with error 0x46
4. Zero-initialize the 0x60-byte node (0x18 dwords)
5. Link node into list:
   - Set node[0x5C] = pListHead[0x0C] (previous head)
   - Set pListHead[0x0C] = pNewNode (new head)
   - Increment pListHead[0x08] (node count)
6. Populate node fields from parameters:
   - node[0x16] = wNodeType
   - node[0x14] = wFlags
   - node[0x24] = dwParam4
   - node[0x28] = dwParam5
   - node[0x2C] = dwParam6
   - node[0x30] = dwParam7
   - node[0x10] = dwParam8
   - node[0x34] = pListHead[0x04] (parent reference)
   - node[0x51] = 2 (status byte)
7. Copy 25 bytes (6 dwords + 1 byte) from pCopyData to node[0x38..0x50]
8. Return pointer to newly allocated node

Parameters:
  pListHead - Pointer to list head structure containing:
              +0x04: Parent reference (copied to node[0x34])
              +0x08: Node count (incremented)
              +0x0C: Head pointer (updated to new node)
  wNodeType - Node type identifier stored at node[0x16]
  wFlags    - Flags stored at node[0x14]
  dwParam4  - Stored at node[0x24]
  dwParam5  - Stored at node[0x28]
  dwParam6  - Stored at node[0x2C]
  dwParam7  - Stored at node[0x30]

functions.name: ProcessTileComponentNodes
functions.comment:

functions.name: AllocateResourceHashTable
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a hash table for resource entries from a GameSessionConfig.

2. If allocation fails, abort with error code 0x2b (43)

5. Loop from 0 to pGameConfig->nEntryCount (offset 0x10c)

functions.comment:

3. Allocate primary table structure (0x22C bytes = 556 bytes)

5. Set table type field to 7, optionally set flag at offset 0x4 if source flag set
6. Store direction count at table offset 0x10C
7. Allocate direction array (count * 0x60 bytes per entry)
8. Zero the direction array memory
9. Loop through source linked list, copying each direction entry via CopyDirectionData
10. Verify copied count matches expected count (abort with 0x247 if mismatch)
11. Return success (0) with table pointer in output parameter

Parameters:
  pDirectionSource - Pointer to source structure containing direction data
    [+0x00] int nFlag - Optional flag (if non-zero, sets table[1]=1)
    [+0x08] int nDirectionCount - Number of directions to copy
    [+0x0C] int pLinkedList - Pointer to linked list of direction entries

Returns:

  0x85200004 - No directions in source (ppOutTable set to NULL)

functions.name: BuildPaletteLayerGrid
functions.comment:
Builds a 5x5 grid of palette layer entries for sprite color transformation.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through 25 grid positions (5x5 grid, 0x19 iterations)
2. Initialize local layer entry buffer with zeros
3. Call FUN_6fe1a080 to populate layer data from palette using grid indices
4. Check flag bit 0x10000 in dwLayerFlags to determine if layer is active
5. If active, encode grid position: X = iVar3 % 5, Y = iVar3 / 5
6. Allocate 20-byte layer entry via Ordinal_10042 (Fog memory allocator)
7. Copy local buffer to allocated entry
8. Link entry into linked list at [EDI+0x58], increment count at [EDI+0x54]
9. Store grid indices from g_adwPaletteGridIndices

Parameters:
  pPaletteData - Pointer to source palette color data
  IMPLICIT EDI - Pointer to parent sprite/graphics context structure

Returns:
  void - Populates linked list in parent structure

Magic Numbers:
  0x19 (25) - Total grid positions (5x5)
  0x10000 - Active layer flag bit
  0x1a7 (423) - Allocation size for layer entry

Error Handling:

functions.name: CopySubEntryColorData
functions.signature: void CopySubEntryColorData(void * this, ColorPalette * pSrcPalette, void * pContext)
functions.comment:
Copies color palette data from a source sub-entry to the destination sub-entry.

If the source has no color data (offset 0x10 is NULL), clears the destination
flags and entry count. Otherwise, calls ConvertColorPaletteEntries to convert
RGB triplets, then validates the converted data by scanning for non-zero entries.

Based on flag bits in the destination (offset 0x8):
- Bit 12 (0x1000): Compression mode - calls FUN_6fe1fdf0 for decompression
- Bit 13 (0x2000): Special processing mode - calls FUN_6fe1fef0
- Neither set: Error 0x43b (invalid encoding mode)

Algorithm:
1. Check if source has color data (pSrcSubEntry->pColorData != NULL)
2. If no data: clear destination flags and return
3. Call ConvertColorPaletteEntries to process RGB data
4. Loop through converted color entries:
   a. Skip zero entries (transparent colors)
   b. Check destination encoding flags
   c. If compression enabled: decompress and validate size
   d. If special mode: call alternate processor
   e. Otherwise: report error 0x43b
5. On success: call InitializeModule and clear destination state

Parameters:
  this (ECX)         - Destination ColorSubEntry structure pointer (0x14 bytes)
  pSrcSubEntry (EAX) - IMPLICIT: Source sub-entry structure pointer
  pSrcPalette        - Source ColorPalette for color conversion
  pContext           - Context/callback parameter for conversion

Returns:
  void - Modifies destination sub-entry in place

Error Codes:
  0x434 - Decompression returned NULL (FUN_6fe1fdf0 failed)
  0x435 - Decompressed size exceeds 0x10000 (65536 bytes)
  0x43b - Invalid encoding mode (neither compression nor special mode)

ColorSubEntry Structure Layout (0x14 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field         Type    Description
  0x00    4     dwField0      dword   Reserved field 0
  0x04    4     dwField1      dword   Reserved field 1
  0x08    2     wFlags        ushort  Encoding flags (bit 12=compress, bit 13=special)
  0x0A    2     wEntryCount   ushort  Number of color entries
  0x0C    4     dwField3      dword   Reserved field 3
  0x10    4     pColorData    void*   Pointer to color data buffer

functions.name: ClearFileContextCache
functions.signature: void ClearFileContextCache(void * this, void * pFileContext, int nReserved)
functions.comment:
Clears and frees all cached entries from a file context structure.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if nReserved is non-zero (indicates reserved/locked state)
2. Validate pFileContext pointer; abort with line 0x25a if NULL
3. Call ClearAllCacheEntries to flush cache for this context
4. If flag 0x4 set in pFileContext+0x4: call InitializeModule and return (special mode)
5. If flag 0x8 set in pFileContext+0x4: abort with line 0x267 (invalid state)
6. Iterate through all categories (count at +0x10c, array at +0x110):
   a. Each category is 0x60 bytes
   b. For each category, iterate entries (count at +0x50, array at +0x54)
   c. Each entry is 0x14 bytes; free memory if +0x10 is non-zero
   d. Clear entry fields (+0xa word, +0x10 dword)
   e. Free category entry array and clear category counts
7. Free category array and reset file context counters

Parameters:
  this (ECX)       - Cache manager instance (IMPLICIT via __thiscall)
  pFileContext     - File context structure containing cached data; NULL causes abort
  nReserved        - Reserved flag; non-zero causes immediate return (skip cleanup)

Returns:
  void - No return value (aborts via CleanupAndAbort on error)

Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field              Description
  0x04    4     dwFlags            Bit 0x4=special mode, 0x8=invalid state
  0x10c   4     nCategoryCount     Number of category slots
  0x110   4     pCategoryArray     Pointer to category array

Magic Numbers:

  0x267 - Assert line for invalid flag 0x8 state
  0x274 - Line number for entry data free
  0x27b - Line number for entry array free
  0x281 - Line number for category array free

functions.signature: void DeepCopyStructure(void * pSrcStruct, void * * ppDestStruct, void * pContext)
functions.comment:

  0x450 - Flag bit 0 not set in source

  0x470 - Zero-size sub-entry allocation
  0x473 - Failed to allocate sub-entries

Initializes a resource buffer from file data, or promotes an existing cache node if already loaded.

2. If cached, call PromoteCacheNode to move to front of LRU and return success
3. If not cached but pFilePath (+0x50) is set:
   a. Allocate buffer via FUN_6fe244f0
   b. Store buffer pointer at pCachedBuffer, data pointer at pDataPointer
   c. Zero-initialize buffer: DWORD-aligned writes (dwBufferSize >> 2), then remaining bytes (dwBufferSize & 3)
   d. Load resource via GetDefaultResourceCount using hResourceHandle
   e. Validate and bind socket using hSocket
   f. Validate async container context
   g. Verify resource loaded (abort if null after successful GetDefaultResourceCount)
   h. Build project path and rebase structure pointers
4. On failure, call GetLastError and log error message

Parameters:

    +0x48 (hSocket): Socket/handle value for ValidateAndBindSocket
    +0x4c (dwBufferSize): Buffer size in bytes (DWORD)
    +0x50 (pFilePath): File path flag/pointer indicating resource exists
    +0x54 (pDataPointer): Data pointer (output - set to buffer data start)
    +0x58 (hResourceHandle): Resource handle for GetDefaultResourceCount
    +0x5c (pCachedBuffer): Cached buffer pointer (output - set to allocated buffer)

  IMPLICIT pCacheEntry (EDI) - Cache entry pointer for PromoteCacheNode

Returns:

  false (0) - Initialization failed:
    - pFilePath is null (no resource to load)
    - GetDefaultResourceCount failed (file open error)

functions.name: AllocateCacheEntryFromFreeList
functions.comment:
Allocates a cache entry node from the sprite cache free list pool.

Algorithm:
1. Load critical section pointer from pool context (EDI+0x30)
2. If critical section is NULL, return NULL immediately
3. Enter critical section for thread safety
4. Check if pool has capacity (count != 0x1400) and sufficient space
5. Remove head node from free list via RemoveHeadFromFreeList
6. Insert node to destination list via InsertNodeToFreeList
7. If allocation fails, call error handler and abort
8. Increment pool counters (EDI+0x0C and EDI+0x08)
9. Leave critical section and return allocated node

  nListSelector (param_1) - List selection passed to InsertNodeToFreeList:

  IMPLICIT pPoolContext (EDI) - Pool control structure containing:

                                +0x08: Current size accumulator
                                +0x0C: Node count (max 0x1400 = 5120)
                                +0x30: LPCRITICAL_SECTION for thread safety
  IMPLICIT nNodeSize (EBX) - Size increment per node allocation

Returns:
  void* - Pointer to allocated cache entry node, or NULL if:
          - Critical section is NULL (pool not initialized)
          - Pool is at maximum capacity (0x1400 nodes)
          - No space remaining in pool
          - RemoveHeadFromFreeList returns NULL

  If RemoveHeadFromFreeList returns NULL after capacity check passed:
  - Calls CleanupAndAbort with source file ref 0x6fe2ec35
  - Line number 0x9C8 (2504) indicates assertion failure
  - ReportError(-1) terminates execution

  Uses Windows CRITICAL_SECTION from pool context for synchronization

functions.name: BuildSpriteFilePath
functions.comment:
Builds the file path for sprite data files based on unit type.

Constructs the full file path to sprite graphics (.dcc or .dc6 format) based on
the unit type and its associated metadata. Uses implicit register parameters:
EBX points to the token string, ESI points to the sprite info structure.

1. Check if token string is empty, return 0 if so

   - 1 (MONSTER): DATA\GLOBAL\MONSTERS\[token1]\[token2]\[name].dcc/dc6
   - 2 (OBJECT): DATA\GLOBAL\OBJECTS\[token1]\[token2]\[name].dcc/dc6
   - 3 (MISSILE): DATA\GLOBAL\MISSILES\[name].dcc
   - 4 (ITEM): DATA\GLOBAL\items\[name].dc6
   - 6 (OVERLAY): DATA\GLOBAL\OVERLAYS\[name].dc6 or .dcc
4. Extract 3-char COF tokens from offsets 0x2c-0x2e and 0x30-0x32
5. Format path with wsprintf and set DCC flag bit if applicable

Parameters:
  szPathBuffer - LPSTR, output buffer for the constructed file path
  IMPLICIT EBX - char*, pointer to file token/name string
  IMPLICIT ESI - SpriteInfo*, pointer to sprite metadata structure

Returns:
  int - 1 if path was built successfully, 0 if failed (empty token or invalid type)

  0x233 (563) - Object class ID forcing DC6 format

functions.comment:
Unlinks a cache entry node from the appropriate doubly-linked list based on flags.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pCacheEntry is not NULL (abort with error 0xB44 if NULL)
2. Check flag bit 0 at pCacheEntry+0x0C to select list type:
   - Bit 0 clear: Use primary list (head at +0x14, tail at +0x18)
   - Bit 0 set: Use secondary list (head at +0x1C, tail at +0x20)
3. If entry is list head:
   a. Check if locked (bit 2 set at +0x0C) - if locked, return early
   b. Get next node from entry+0x14
   c. Update container head pointer to next node
   d. If next is NULL, also clear container tail pointer
   e. Clear entry prev/next pointers to NULL
4. If entry is list tail:
   a. Get prev node from entry+0x18
   b. Update container tail pointer to prev node
   c. Clear prev node next pointer and entry pointers
5. If entry is in middle of list:
   a. Unlink by bridging prev/next nodes together
   b. Clear entry prev/next pointers

- pContainer (ECX): Pointer to cache list container structure

Returns:

- NULL pCacheEntry triggers fatal error (line 0xB44)
- Locked entries (bit 2 set) are skipped without unlinking
- Empty list (head is NULL) returns immediately

functions.name: CleanupSpriteCacheManager
functions.comment:
Cleans up and destroys a sprite cache manager, freeing all cached entries and resources.

Algorithm:
1. Check if cache entry count (ESI+0x0C) is non-zero
2. For each cache entry in the manager:
   a. Get next entry from secondary list (ESI+0x1C) or primary list (ESI+0x14)
   b. If both lists have entries, call UnlinkCacheEntryFromList to choose
   c. Check entry flags (offset +0x0C) for bit 0x2 (locked/in-use) - skip if set
   d. Enter critical section (ESI+0x30) for thread safety
   e. Subtract entry size from total cache size (ESI+0x08)
   f. Leave critical section
   g. If entry has eviction callback (offset +0x08), invoke it via ESI+0x2C
   h. If entry has resource buffer (offset +0x00), call DeallocateResourceBuffer
   i. Add entry to free list (ESI+0x24/0x28)
   j. Decrement entry count and continue if more entries remain
3. If auxiliary buffer exists (ESI+0x10), deallocate it
4. If critical section initialized (ESI+0x30):
   a. Call DeleteCriticalSection
   b. Call InitializeModule for cleanup
   c. Clear critical section pointer

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT ESI: SpriteListData* - Pointer to sprite cache manager structure
  IMPLICIT EDI: SpriteListData* - Secondary sprite list context for UnlinkCacheEntryFromList

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - Entries with flag bit 0x2 set are skipped (locked/in-use entries)
  - Empty cache (count == 0) exits immediately
  - NULL critical section pointer skips lock operations
  - Eviction callbacks invoked before resource deallocation

Magic Numbers:
  0x2 - Entry locked flag in flags field (offset +0x0C)
  0xa22, 0x94b, 0x95d - Resource identifiers for DeallocateResourceBuffer
  0x6fe2ef28 - Static resource context pointer

functions.name: InitSpriteCacheFrameSlots
functions.comment:
Initializes sprite cache frame slots for animation frame storage.

Allocates memory for sprite frame slot structures and links each frame
entry in the sprite data to its corresponding cache slot. Validates
frame data integrity before assignment.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters (nResourceContext and pSpriteHeader must be non-null)
2. Check sprite flags for initialization state (bit 0 must be clear)
3. Verify sprite header not already initialized (offset +0x28 == 0)
4. Extract frame count (bFramesPerDir at +0x21) and direction count (bDirectionCount at +0x24)
5. Allocate frame slot array via Ordinal_10045 (size = directions * frames * 0x2C)
6. Zero-initialize allocated memory using DWORD-aligned memset pattern
7. Validate entity state via ValidateEntityState() on sprite data pointer (+0xB0)
8. Iterate through all frames: validate frame header, link slot pointer at +0x18
9. Advance frame offset by frame data size (0x23 + sizes at +0x14 and +0x1C)
10. Mark header as initialized by setting +0x28 = 1

Parameters:
  pbFlags       - byte* - Pointer to sprite flags byte (bit 0 = skip init flag)
  nResourceContext - int - Resource context handle for error reporting
  IMPLICIT pSpriteHeader - int (EAX) - Pointer to sprite animation header structure

Returns:
  void - No return value; aborts on error via CleanupAndAbort()

Error Codes:
  0x519 - NULL resource context
  0x51A - NULL sprite header
  0x51B - Sprite flags indicate already initialized (bit 0 set)
  0x51E - Sprite already has frame slots allocated (+0x28 != 0)
  0x530 - ValidateEntityState failed on sprite data
  0x5AE - Frame data validation failed (corrupt header/oversized dimensions)

Sprite Header Structure Layout (offsets from pSpriteHeader):
  +0x21  byte   bFramesPerDir  - Animation frames per direction
  +0x22  byte   bCurrentDir    - Current direction index for frame table
  +0x24  byte   bDirectionCount - Total animation directions
  +0x28  int    nInitialized   - Initialization flag (0=not init, 1=init)
  +0x2C  int[]  aFrameOffsets  - Array of frame data offsets per direction
  +0xB0  void*  pSpriteData    - Pointer to raw sprite data buffer

Frame Slot Entry (0x2C bytes each):
  +0x00  int    nFrameFlags    - Frame header flags (must be 0)
  +0x04  uint   dwWidth        - Frame width (must be <= 0x100)
  +0x08  uint   dwHeight       - Frame height (must be <= 0x100)
  +0x14  int    nDataSize1     - Additional data block 1 size
  +0x18  ptr    pCacheSlot     - Pointer to cache slot (assigned by this function)
  +0x1C  int    nDataSize2     - Additional data block 2 size

Source File: ..\Source\D2CMP\SRC\SpriteCache.cpp (line ~0x523)

functions.name: GetSkillSlotEntry
functions.signature: int * GetSkillSlotEntry(int * pSkillsBuffer, SkillSlotDescriptor * pSlotDesc, int * pSkillInstance)
functions.comment:
Retrieves a skill slot entry from the skills buffer based on skill type and slot index.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSkillsBuffer and pSlotDesc are non-NULL
2. Check slot index against max slots (pSlotDesc->nMaxSlots > pSkillInstance[0x11])
3. Determine slot offset based on skill type (pSkillInstance[7]):
   - Type 2: Use offset 0 (first slot)
   - Type 4: Use owner ID from pSkillInstance[0] as offset
   - Type 6 with flag 0x2: Call Ordinal_10069 for slot index lookup
   - Other: Use pSkillsBuffer as base
4. Validate slot offset against max and retrieve offset from pSlotDesc->adwOffsets table
5. Iterate through slots, validating each entry structure
6. Return pointer to matching slot entry or NULL on error

Parameters:
  pSkillsBuffer (EBX) - Base pointer to skills data buffer
  pSlotDesc (EAX) - SkillSlotDescriptor* with nMaxSlots at +4, nSlotCount at +3, adwOffsets at +0xc
  pSkillInstance (ECX) - Skill instance with type at +0x1c, flags at +0x18, owner at +0, slot index at +0x44

Returns:
  int* - Pointer to skill slot entry structure, or NULL if:
    - Any input pointer is NULL
    - Slot index exceeds max slots
    - Offset is negative or out of range
    - Entry validation fails (non-zero first field, width/height > 0x100)

Slot Entry Structure Layout:
  Offset  Size  Field         Type    Description
  0x00    4     dwReserved    uint    Must be 0 for valid entry
  0x04    4     dwWidth       uint    Entry width (must be <= 0x100)
  0x08    4     dwHeight      uint    Entry height (must be <= 0x100)
  0x14    4     nDataLen1     int     First variable data length
  0x1C    4     nDataLen2     int     Second variable data length
  Entry size: 0x23 + nDataLen1 + nDataLen2

Skill Type Constants:
  2 - First slot (offset 0)
  4 - Owner-based slot (uses owner ID)
  6 - Dynamic slot (uses Ordinal_10069 lookup)

functions.name: FormatStringWithGameSuffix
functions.signature: void FormatStringWithGameSuffix(char * lpszBuffer, int nUseDefault, char * lpszFormat, va_list args)
functions.comment:
Formats a string using vsprintf and appends a game-specific suffix.

Selects between default and fallback game string pointers based on the
nUseDefault flag and whether pdwResult_6fe3011c is valid. After formatting,
appends the suffix using an optimized copy (4-byte chunks then remaining bytes).

Algorithm:
1. Call _vsprintf to format lpszFormat with args into lpszBuffer
2. Select suffix string: if nUseDefault==0 OR pdwResult is NULL, use fallback
3. Calculate suffix string length via strlen loop
4. Find end of formatted buffer via strlen loop
5. Copy suffix to buffer end using optimized memcpy:
   a. Copy dwords (4-byte chunks) while dwDwordCount > 0
   b. Copy remaining bytes (0-3) individually

Parameters:
  lpszBuffer  - [out] Destination buffer for formatted string with suffix
  nUseDefault - [in]  If 0, always use fallback; otherwise use default if valid
  lpszFormat  - [in]  printf-style format string
  args        - [in]  va_list of format arguments

Returns:
  void - Result stored in lpszBuffer (must be caller-allocated with sufficient size)

Special Cases:
  - pdwResult_6fe3011c == NULL: Forces use of g_pFallbackGamePtr regardless of nUseDefault
  - Empty suffix string: No bytes appended after vsprintf output

Globals:
  g_pDefaultGamePtr   - Primary game suffix string pointer
  g_pFallbackGamePtr  - Fallback game suffix string pointer
  pdwResult_6fe3011c  - Validity check pointer (NULL = invalid state)

functions.name: UpdateSpriteCacheState
functions.comment:
Updates sprite cache memory tracking after storing new decompressed data.

Algorithm:
1. Check if cache context has a valid critical section (exit if null)
2. Enter critical section to protect cache state modifications
3. Subtract old entry size from total cache size (pCacheContext+8)
4. Calculate new entry size: nNewDataSize + old size
5. Update cache entry size at pCacheEntry[1]
6. Set in-use flag (bit 1) at pCacheEntry[3] to prevent eviction
7. Add new entry size to total cache size
8. Leave critical section
9. If cache exceeds capacity (pCacheContext+4 < total):
   a. Call FUN_6fe1bde0 to get LRU entry for eviction
   b. If no entry available, break eviction loop
   c. If evicted entry is our entry, abort (self-eviction error)
   d. Re-check cache size under lock, continue if still over capacity
10. Clear in-use flag (bit 1) at pCacheEntry[3]
11. Leave critical section and return

Parameters:
  nNewDataSize: int - New size of decompressed sprite data to add to cache
  IMPLICIT pCacheContext (EAX): pointer - Sprite cache context structure
  IMPLICIT pCacheEntry (EDI): pointer - Cache entry being updated

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - Returns immediately if pCacheContext+0x30 is NULL (no critical section)
  - Aborts via CleanupAndAbort if self-eviction detected (line 0xA89)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x30: Offset to LPCRITICAL_SECTION in cache context
  0x08: Offset to total cache size in cache context
  0x04: Offset to maximum cache capacity in cache context
  0x02: In-use flag bit mask (pCacheEntry[3])
  0xFFFFFFFD: Mask to clear in-use flag
  0xA89 (2697): Source line number for error reporting
  0x6FE2EC35: Pointer to source file path string

Error Handling:
  - Self-eviction triggers fatal error: CleanupAndAbort followed by ReportError(-1)

Structure Layout (Cache Context at pCacheContext):
  Offset  Size  Type                  Description
  0x04    0x04  uint                  Maximum cache capacity
  0x08    0x04  uint                  Current total cache size
  0x30    0x04  LPCRITICAL_SECTION    Critical section for thread safety

Structure Layout (Cache Entry at pCacheEntry):
  Offset  Size  Type   Description
  0x04    0x04  uint   Entry data size (pCacheEntry[1])
  0x0C    0x04  uint   Status flags (pCacheEntry[3]), bit 1 = in-use

functions.name: GetValidatedSkillSlotEntry
functions.comment:
Retrieves a validated skill slot entry from an entity's skill buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSkillInstance is non-NULL
2. Validate entity pointer at pSkillInstance[0x2c] (offset 0xB0) is non-NULL
3. Call ValidateEntityState to verify entity is valid and get skills buffer
4. If validation fails, return NULL
5. Copy slot index byte from pSkillInstance+9 (offset 0x24) to output buffer at pOutputSlot[1]
6. Call GetSkillSlotEntry with validated entity, slot descriptor, and output buffer
7. Return skill slot entry pointer or NULL on failure

Parameters:
  pSpriteContext (EBX) - void* - Unused in this function (preserved for register convention)
  pSkillInstance (EAX) - int* - Pointer to skill instance structure:
    +0x20 (offset 8 as int*): SkillSlotDescriptor* pSlotDesc
    +0x24 (offset 9 as int*): byte slot index value
    +0xB0 (offset 0x2C as int*): void* entity pointer for validation
  IMPLICIT pOutputSlot (EDI) - int* - Output buffer for skill slot data:
    +0x04: Receives slot index value from pSkillInstance+0x24

Returns:
  int* - Pointer to skill slot entry structure on success
  NULL (0x0) - On any validation failure:
    - pSkillInstance is NULL
    - Entity pointer at pSkillInstance[0x2C] is NULL
    - ValidateEntityState fails
    - GetSkillSlotEntry fails

  EAX - Input: pSkillInstance pointer
  EBX - Input: pSpriteContext (unused)
  EDI - Input/Output: pOutputSlot buffer (receives slot index at +4)

  Callees: ValidateEntityState (6fe18db2), GetSkillSlotEntry (6fe1c3c0)

functions.name: LoadSpriteDataBlock
functions.signature: byte * LoadSpriteDataBlock(void * this, void * pSpriteCache, int pSpriteConfig, char * szOutputPath)
functions.comment:
Loads sprite data block from cache or initializes new sprite data.

This function retrieves or creates sprite data blocks used for rendering game graphics.
It first attempts to find existing cached data, and if not found, creates and
initializes a new sprite data structure with frame and direction information.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output path buffer to empty string
2. Build sprite identifier path using cache context and sprite config
3. Check cache for existing sprite data block (FUN_6fe21ca0)
4. If cached: retrieve existing data block, skip to return
5. If not cached: build path and create new cache entry (FUN_6fe21c20)
6. Allocate sprite data structure (FUN_6fe244f0), zero-initialize 0x30 dwords (192 bytes)
7. Copy source path string to sprite data buffer at offset 0xa0
8. If sprite config flag bit 0 clear:
   a. Read sprite header dimensions via GetDefaultResourceCount
   b. Populate sprite structure with dimensions at offsets +0x4 through +0x18
   c. Validate tile dimensions (max 0x3fff total tiles)
   d. Read frame data into g_adwFrameDataBuffer
   e. Copy frame offsets to sprite data at offset +0x1c
9. If sprite config flag bit 0 set: call FUN_6fe1d720 for alternate processing
10. Return pointer to sprite data block, or abort with error codes

Parameters:
  this (ECX)         - Sprite cache context pointer (implicit __thiscall)
  pSpriteCache       - Sprite configuration structure with flags at +0x10
  pSpriteConfig      - Output path buffer for sprite identifier
  szOutputPath       - Unused in current implementation

Returns:
  byte* - Pointer to sprite data block structure on success, NULL on failure

Error Codes:
  0x41c - Cache entry allocation failed
  0x421 - Sprite data structure allocation failed  
  0x44d - Tile count exceeds maximum (0x3fff tiles)
  0x452 - Direction count exceeds maximum (0x20)
  0x465 - Sprite data block pointer is null

Structure Layout (Sprite Data Block):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type      Description
  0x00    0x01  flags           byte      Status flags, bit 0 = alternate mode
  0x04    0x04  spriteWidth     uint      Width in pixels
  0x08    0x04  spriteHeight    uint      Height in pixels
  0x0c    0x04  frameCount      uint      Number of animation frames
  0x14    0x04  directionCount  uint      Number of direction variants
  0x18    0x04  tileWidth       uint      Tile width for frame lookup
  0x1c    var   frameOffsets[]  uint[]    Array of frame data offsets

Globals Referenced:
  0x6fe75e50 - Sprite cache table base address
  g_adwFrameDataBuffer (0x6fe87398) - Temporary buffer for frame data

functions.name: ResetSpriteCacheSystem
functions.comment:
Resets the sprite cache system to its initial state.

2. Zero out g_adwSpriteCacheListState array (15 DWORDs at 0x6fe76e50)

Returns:

Special Cases:
- When fClearCacheEntries is FALSE, only state arrays are zeroed (partial reset)
- Critical section deletion only occurs if g_dwSpriteDecompressionLockInitialized was previously set
- Uses REP STOSD for efficient memory zeroing

functions.name: InvalidateAndFreeSpriteNode
functions.comment:
Invalidates and frees a sprite cache entry from the LRU hash table.

This wrapper function handles the removal of a sprite cache entry by clearing its
timestamp (invalidating it) and then calling UnlinkAndFreeHashNode to unlink the
entry from its bucket chain and deallocate the memory.

functions.name: ReleaseSpriteEntry
functions.comment:
Releases a sprite entry and frees its resources.

Algorithm:
1. If sprite resource release callback is set:
   a. Validate sprite has associated resource data (offset 0x20)
   b. Call callback with resource pointer (offset 0x24 of resource data)
   c. If no resource data, report error (line 0xB3)
2. Validate entry pointer is not NULL (reports error line 0x141)
3. Unlink entry from doubly-linked list:
   a. Update prev->next pointer (offset 0x2C) to skip this entry
   b. Update next->prev pointer (offset 0x28) to skip this entry
4. Call FreeSpriteEntry to deallocate entry memory

  IMPLICIT __fastcall: passed via ECX register

  - Entry pointer is NULL (line 0x141)
- Calls ReportError(-1) after cleanup

0x20   | 4    | dwField20  | uint  | Pointer to resource data structure
0x28   | 4    | dwSlotCount| uint  | Pointer to previous entry (linked list)
0x2C   | 4    | dwField2C  | uint  | Pointer to next entry (linked list)
